trust_decision.summary: Whether a checkpoint file loaded with torch.load (full pickle) is trusted to only contain tensors; at the pinned commit no load restricts unpickling (no weights_only / safe loader) anywhere, and the published fix only adds map_location, which does not restrict unpickling.

landing_point.why: Advisory title names 'resnet'; the only torch.load in model/resnet.py is resnet._init_modules loading self.model_path.

fix_sites.entry_point: resnet(...)._init_modules() via _FPN.__init__ (model/fpn.py:86) when pretrained=True; module imports model.fpn.fpn and model.utils.config (model/resnet.py:12-13) which do not exist in the tree, so no reachable CLI uses it
fix_sites.module_kind: library model-definition module (dead/unimportable at pinned commit)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: Published fix touches one line; it adds map_location only (fix.diff:13-15).

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The CLI scripts (demo.py, fddb_test.py, widerface_val.py) load a user-supplied --trained_model, so a solver could argue the user chooses that file and it is 'their own' weights, outside the 'resnet' advisory.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Loading the legitimate released state_dict checkpoints (.pth/.pkl) onto CPU or GPU must keep working; a fix that refuses all pickle/torch.load or drops map_location would break inference.

O6_input_shapes: filesystem path to a .pth checkpoint (string, hardcoded self.model_path at model/resnet.py:219)
